az_lower_devil_s_canyon.blurb: Lower Devil's Canyon is one of the larger sections of Queen Creek Canyon in central Arizona, and it is often called the best climbing in the whole canyon. Trad leads the way, with a solid block of sport routes and only a couple of top-ropes. Grades start at the easy fives and top out around 5.12, with the bulk landing between 5.8 and 5.10 and a smaller group of harder sport lines. The Refuge is the biggest cluster, followed by Lower Devil's East, the Glitter Box Area and Hackberry Creek. Hackberry Creek blends trad, mixed and sport lines on both sides of a small stream, with a waterfall partway along it. Because getting in is demanding, the canyon sees fewer climbers than its neighbors and tends to feel quiet.

ar_big_piney_region.blurb: The Big Piney Region sits in the Ozarks of north-central Arkansas, west of Highway 7 between Dover and Deer, along a river with a turquoise tint and forested sandstone bluffs. Sport routes make up roughly two thirds of the climbing, bouldering about a quarter, and trad is a small extra. The sport is steep and powerful, mostly 5.11 to 5.13 with a handful of moderates mixed in, while the boulder problems run from V0 to V9, most of them in the V1 to V5 range. Rock Creek is the largest sector, a cliff band roughly 50 to 80 feet tall that is still growing. Hurricane Creek holds many of the boulders, and Piney Bowl faces east, so it gets morning sun and drops into shade by late morning. Shoulder seasons and cool winter days suit it best.

ga_boat_rock.blurb: Boat Rock is a small urban boulderfield in southwest Atlanta, stretching close to a mile through a residential district. The boulders are sharp, egg-shaped granite, and nearly everything here is bouldering, with just a few trad lines. Most problems are slabs that reward balance and careful footwork, with some overhanging lines and several crack problems, and a few are tall enough that spotters and extra pads matter. Grades run from V0 up to about V10, with most problems between V0 and V5 and a good number of moderates. The biggest groupings are the Easy Crack Area, the Paint Can and Lost Digits Area, the Beam Me Up Scotty Area and the Half Pipe Area. It has a reputation for being demanding on skin and rubber, and for sharpening technique.

al_sand_rock.blurb: Sand Rock, also known as Cherokee Rock Village, is a sandstone climbing area in Cherokee County in northeast Alabama, near Leesburg. It sits on the southern tip of Lookout Mountain with views over Weiss Lake. The rock is sandstone with a fair bit of conglomerate mixed in, shaped into house-sized boulders, free-standing pinnacles and walls up to about 200 feet. Sport and trad are close to evenly split, with a smaller but real helping of bouldering and a few top-ropes. Grades span the easy fives to 5.13, with most routes between 5.8 and 5.12. Walk-ins are very short and the sectors are spread out enough to find a quiet corner. Sun Wall, Turtle Rock, the Grotto and Holiday Block are the largest. The holds can snap when wet, so dry days are best.

co_empire.blurb: Empire is a small mountain town off I-70 west of Denver, and the climbing above it is alpine granite at roughly 8,600 feet and higher. Sport routes and boulder problems split most of the climbing, with a little trad and a few alpine lines. The sport grades cluster from 5.10 to 5.12, while the boulders cover everything from V0 through the double digits. Rock quality is often good and steep, but the edges are sharp and loose stone turns up, so a helmet is wise. The Ziggurat, the Halidome and Goat Rock hold the walls, and the Northeast Boulders and Vasquez Boulders hold the problems. The Halidome is a south-facing crag over 500 feet tall. The season runs longer than the elevation suggests, with climbing possible into December.

ut_big_water_boulders.blurb: Big Water Boulders is a bouldering field in the Glen Canyon region of southern Utah, near the town of Big Water at about 4,000 feet. The blocks are sandstone that tumbled from the Straight Cliffs onto gray shale below. Quality is uneven: much of the rock is crumbly, and the dark varnished stone is the good stuff. The climbing is mostly slabby, with crimpy faces, pockets and compression, and overhangs are rare. Problems are overwhelmingly easy to moderate, mostly V0 to V3, with only a few above V5, and landings are sandy and soft. The Roadside Boulders, the Moon and the Jupiter area are the main groupings. It is quiet and works well for beginners and families. Early spring, late fall and winter are best, since summer is very hot.
